subjects.title: Maths
subjects.framework: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

units.title: Big numbers
goals: Read and write numbers up to a million in digits, in words and in expanded form
Explain why a digit is worth ten times as much as the same digit one place to its right

units.title: Compare and round
goals: Compare big numbers with >, < and =
Round big numbers to any place

units.title: Add and subtract big numbers
goals: Add and subtract numbers up to a million in columns
Solve story problems with more than one step and check that the answer makes sense

units.title: Times as many
goals: Read 35 = 5 × 7 as "35 is 5 times as many as 7"
Solve story problems that compare with times as many

units.title: Multiply bigger numbers
goals: Multiply a number of up to four digits by a one-digit number
Multiply two two-digit numbers with place value and area models

units.title: Divide with remainders
goals: Divide numbers of up to four digits by a one-digit number
Find remainders and decide what they mean in a story

units.title: Factors, multiples and primes
goals: Find all the factor pairs of a number up to 100
Tell whether a number is a multiple of another
Tell whether a number is prime or composite

units.title: Patterns and rules
goals: Continue a number or shape pattern from its rule
Notice things about a pattern that the rule does not say

units.title: Equal fractions
goals: Make equivalent fractions by multiplying the top and the bottom by the same number
Compare fractions with different denominators, using 1/2 as a benchmark

units.title: Add and subtract fractions
goals: Add and subtract fractions with the same denominator
Split a fraction into a sum of smaller fractions
Add and subtract mixed numbers

units.title: Fractions times whole numbers
goals: See a fraction like 3/4 as 3 × 1/4
Multiply a fraction by a whole number in stories

units.title: Tenths and hundredths
goals: Write tenths as hundredths and add them
Write fractions with 10 or 100 on the bottom as decimals
Compare decimals to hundredths

units.title: Measure and convert
goals: Know how big km, m, cm, kg, g, L, mL, hours, minutes and seconds are
Change a bigger unit into a smaller one
Solve stories about distance, time, capacity, mass and gold

units.title: Area and perimeter
goals: Find the area and the perimeter of rectangles
Find a missing side from the area or the perimeter

units.title: Line plots
goals: Show measurements in fractions of a unit on a line plot
Answer questions from a line plot by adding and subtracting fractions

units.title: Angles
goals: Know that angles are measured in degrees and a full turn is 360 degrees
Measure and draw angles
Add angles and find a missing angle

units.title: Lines, shapes and symmetry
goals: Name points, lines, segments, rays, parallel and perpendicular lines, and right, acute and obtuse angles
Sort shapes by their sides and angles
Find lines of symmetry

units.title: Tables, line graphs and pie charts
standards: SG P4 tables, line graphs, pie charts
goals: Read and complete tables
Read line graphs that show change over time
Read simple pie charts

units.title: Energy and speed
goals: Explain that a faster object has more energy
Describe what happens to energy when things bump into each other

units.title: Energy on the move
goals: Show that energy moves from place to place by sound, light, heat and electric currents
Design a simple device that changes energy from one form into another

units.title: Electric circuits
goals: Build a circuit with a cell, wires, a bulb and a switch
Tell conductors from insulators
Use electricity safely

units.title: Heat and temperature
goals: Measure temperature with a thermometer
Explain that heat flows from hotter to colder things
Tell good and poor conductors of heat

units.title: Solids, liquids and gases
goals: Group materials by state
Know melting and freezing points
Explain evaporation and condensation

units.title: Sound and hearing
goals: Explain that sounds are vibrations travelling to the ear
Change the pitch and volume of a sound

units.title: Waves
goals: Describe waves by how tall they are and how far apart they are
Show that waves can make things move

units.title: Light and seeing
goals: Explain that we see things when light bounces off them into our eyes

units.title: Sending messages with patterns
goals: Compare ways to send information with patterns, like codes and signals

units.title: Plant and animal parts
goals: Explain how the inside and outside parts of plants and animals help them live, grow and have young

units.title: Digestion and teeth
goals: Name the parts of the digestive system and what they do
Name the types of teeth and how to care for them

units.title: Senses and the brain
goals: Explain how animals take in information with their senses and use it to act

units.title: Rock layers and fossils
goals: Explain how rock layers form, with the oldest at the bottom
Use fossils to tell how a place has changed over a very long time

units.title: Weathering and erosion
goals: Explain how water, ice, wind and plants break rock down and carry it away

units.title: Mapping Earth's features
goals: Find patterns of mountains, volcanoes, earthquakes and ocean floors on maps

units.title: Energy resources
goals: Tell renewable from non-renewable energy resources and how using them changes the environment

units.title: Natural hazards
goals: Compare ways to reduce the harm of earthquakes, floods and volcanoes

units.title: How rockets work
goals: Explain how a rocket's push sends it up
Tell why a rocket carries its own oxygen and drops its stages

units.title: Stories: characters and theme
goals: Describe a character using details from the story
Find the theme of a story
Use details from the story to answer questions about what happened

units.title: Reading to learn: the main idea
goals: Find the main idea of a text and the details that support it
Summarise a text

units.title: How texts are built
goals: Tell whether a text uses time order, compare and contrast, cause and effect, or problem and solution

units.title: Poems, plays and stories
goals: Tell poems, plays and stories apart by their parts
Tell a story told by "I" from a story told by someone outside it

units.title: Myths and traditional tales
goals: Compare themes and patterns in tales from different cultures
Understand phrases that come from old stories (a Herculean task)

units.title: Accounts, reasons and evidence
goals: Compare a first-hand and a second-hand account of the same event
Explain how a writer uses reasons and evidence

units.title: Words that sound alike
goals: Choose between to, too and two; there, their and they're; and other words that sound alike

units.title: Word parts: prefixes, suffixes and roots
goals: Use prefixes, suffixes and Greek and Latin roots to work out what words mean

units.title: Context clues
goals: Use the words around a new word to work out what it means
Find synonyms and antonyms

units.title: Similes, metaphors and idioms
goals: Explain similes and metaphors
Know common idioms, sayings and proverbs

units.title: Complete sentences
goals: Find and fix sentence fragments and run-on sentences

units.title: Verbs: -ing tenses and helping verbs
goals: Use the progressive tenses: I was walking, I am walking, I will be walking
Use can, may and must

units.title: Adjectives and prepositions
goals: Put adjectives in the usual order: a small old wooden box
Use prepositional phrases

units.title: Who, which, that, where, when
goals: Use relative pronouns and relative adverbs to join ideas

units.title: Capitals, commas and quotation marks
goals: Use capital letters correctly
Punctuate what people say with quotation marks and commas
Put a comma before and, but or so when joining two sentences

units.title: Write an opinion
goals: State an opinion
Give reasons backed by facts
Link ideas (for example, in addition) and end with a conclusion

units.title: Research and report
goals: Take notes from a few sources
Write a report with headings, facts and a conclusion

units.title: Write a narrative
goals: Tell events in a clear order with dialogue and description
Use words that show time and feelings
Write a good ending

subjects.title: History
subjects.framework: England's National Curriculum (KS2-KS3) with California world history, Cambridge Humanities and C3

units.title: The first cities
goals: Explain why the first cities grew beside rivers
Say what makes a civilisation

units.title: Sumer and the first writing
goals: Describe cuneiform writing, the wheel and city-states

units.title: Ancient Egypt
goals: Describe life by the Nile
Explain pharaohs, pyramids and hieroglyphs

units.title: The Indus Valley
goals: Describe planned cities with drains and baths, such as Mohenjo-daro

units.title: Shang Dynasty China
goals: Describe bronze work, oracle bones and early Chinese writing

units.title: Kush and Nubia
goals: Describe the kingdom south of Egypt, its pyramids and its trade

units.title: Farming, trade and the first money
goals: Explain how spare food, trade and the first money changed life

units.title: How ancient people counted
standards: UK KS2 (achievements of the earliest civilisations)
goals: Compare Egyptian and Babylonian numbers
Explain why an hour has 60 minutes

units.title: How archaeologists work
goals: Describe digging, dating and caring for finds
Say what finds can and cannot tell us

units.title: Comparing civilisations
standards: UK KS2 (where and when the first civilisations appeared)
goals: Compare the first civilisations by river, writing, leaders and inventions

subjects.title: Geography
subjects.framework: England's National Curriculum (KS2-KS3) with Cambridge Humanities and C3

units.title: Countries and capitals
goals: Find major countries and capitals on each continent

units.title: Europe
goals: Find Europe's countries, seas, rivers and mountains

units.title: North and South America
goals: Find the countries, the Andes, the Rockies and the Amazon

units.title: Rivers
goals: Follow a river from source to mouth
Explain why rivers matter to people

units.title: Mountains
goals: Explain how mountains form
Describe life in the mountains

units.title: Volcanoes and earthquakes
goals: Explain where and why they happen
Describe how people prepare

units.title: Water on the move
goals: Explain the water cycle
Say where fresh water comes from

units.title: Scale and distance
goals: Use a map scale to find real distances

units.title: Two regions compared
goals: Compare the land, weather, work and towns of two regions (one in Europe, one in the Americas)

units.title: Fieldwork
goals: Collect data outdoors (land use, traffic, weather) and present it

subjects.title: Citizenship
subjects.framework: England's citizenship, C3 civics and economics, Jump$tart, Japan's and Finland's ethics

units.title: Rights and responsibilities
goals: Know that every child has rights (the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child)
Explain that rights come with responsibilities

units.title: Who runs a town?
standards: J$ SP 4 (sharing costs in a community)
goals: Explain what a local council does
Name services we pay for together (roads, parks, libraries)

units.title: Deciding together
goals: Compare voting, taking turns and agreeing
Choose a fair way for a decision

units.title: Keep going
goals: Learn from mistakes
Break a hard goal into steps

units.title: In someone else's shoes
goals: Notice how others feel
Include people who are left out

units.title: Standing up to bullying
goals: Say what bullying is, including online
Know how to get help and how to help others safely

units.title: Smart spending
goals: Compare prices
Weigh costs and benefits
Explain opportunity cost

units.title: Adverts and you
goals: Explain how adverts try to persuade
Notice when friends make you want things

units.title: Ways to pay
goals: Compare cash, cards and phone payments
Explain that money is real even when you cannot see it

units.title: Helping your community
goals: Name ways children can help
Plan a small helping project

units.title: Big questions: is it ever OK to…?
goals: Discuss a dilemma and give reasons
Change your mind when you hear a better reason

subjects.title: Computing
subjects.framework: England's computing with CSTA, Cambridge Computing and Digital Literacy, Estonia and Korea

units.title: Events
goals: Make things happen when something is tapped or touched

units.title: If… then… else
goals: Use if-then-else to make choices in a program

units.title: Variables
goals: Use a variable to keep a score

units.title: Plan before you code
goals: Plan a program with steps or a flowchart

units.title: Networks
goals: Explain how computers connect
Say what a router and a server do

units.title: Search smart
goals: Choose good search words
Explain that results are ranked

units.title: Is it true?
standards: UK KS2 (be discerning in evaluating digital content)
goals: Check information online: who wrote it, when and why

units.title: Data in tables
goals: Sort and filter a table to answer a question

units.title: Your digital footprint
goals: Explain that what you share can stay online
Think before you post

units.title: Getting help online
goals: Block, report and tell a trusted adult
Tell OK from not-OK behaviour online

units.title: Computers that changed the world
goals: Describe how computers changed work and play, from room-sized machines to phones

subjects.title: Art and Design
subjects.framework: England's Art and Design with the National Core Arts Standards and Cambridge

units.title: The colour wheel
goals: Use primary, secondary and complementary colours
Tell warm from cool colours

units.title: Light and shade
goals: Shade to make things look solid
Make a scale of tones

units.title: Portraits and faces
goals: Draw a face in proportion
Look at portraits by great artists

units.title: Landscapes
goals: Paint a landscape with foreground, middle ground and background

units.title: Art of the first civilisations
goals: Use the rules and patterns of Egyptian art
Design with symbols like hieroglyphs

units.title: Printmaking
goals: Make a relief print with a repeating motif

units.title: Relief sculpture
goals: Make a sculpture that stands out from a wall

units.title: Pixel art
standards: CAM DL tools and content creation
goals: Make a picture on a grid
Explain colours and resolution

units.title: Talking about art
goals: Give kind, useful feedback ("I like… I wonder…")
Improve your work from feedback

subjects.title: Music
subjects.framework: England's Music with the National Core Arts Standards

units.title: Note values
goals: Read semibreves, minims, crotchets and quavers (whole, half, quarter, eighth notes)
Count beats in a bar

units.title: Beats in a bar
goals: Feel 2, 3 and 4 beats in a bar
Tell a march from a waltz

units.title: Notes on the stave
goals: Read notes on the treble stave from C to C

units.title: Compose a melody
goals: Make a melody from five notes (pentatonic) with steps and leaps

units.title: Layers and ostinato
goals: Repeat a pattern under a melody
Build music in layers

units.title: The orchestra
goals: Name where instruments sit and how they sound

units.title: Rounds and part-singing
goals: Sing a round in two or three parts

units.title: Music long ago
goals: Describe the first instruments (bone flutes, lyres, drums)

units.title: Music for moving pictures
goals: Explain how music sets the mood in films and games

subjects.title: Health and PE
subjects.framework: England's PE and health education, SHAPE America, the National Health Education Standards and CASEL

units.title: Striking and fielding
goals: Hit, field and throw accurately in bat-and-ball games

units.title: Attack and defend
goals: Keep the ball, find space and defend a goal

units.title: Gymnastics sequences
goals: Link rolls, balances and jumps smoothly

units.title: Athletics
goals: Sprint, run a relay, jump and throw for distance
Measure and improve

units.title: Parts of fitness
goals: Name stamina, strength, speed and flexibility
Warm up and cool down

units.title: Reading food labels
goals: Find sugar, salt and fat on a label
Choose drinks wisely

units.title: Big feelings
goals: Handle anger, worry and sadness with strategies that work

units.title: Safe and unsafe
goals: Tell safe from unsafe secrets
Name your trusted adults

units.title: Water safety
standards: UK KS2 swimming and water safety
goals: Read beach flags
Know how to float and call for help

units.title: First aid basics
goals: Know what to do for cuts, bumps and burns
Know when to get an adult

units.title: Outdoor adventure
standards: UK KS2 outdoor and adventurous activity
goals: Follow a map to find markers
Solve team challenges

subjects.title: Design and Technology
subjects.framework: England's Design and Technology with Finland's, Estonia's and Japan's crafts and home economics

units.title: Electrical products
goals: Design a product with a circuit and a switch (a torch, an alarm)

units.title: Wheels and axles
goals: Build a vehicle with wheels and axles that rolls straight

units.title: Make a bag
goals: Design, cut and sew a simple bag

units.title: Shelters and frames
goals: Build a shelter that stands up to the wind

units.title: Bread and grains
goals: Explain how wheat becomes flour and bread
Explain what yeast does

units.title: Plan a balanced meal
goals: Plan a meal with every food group

units.title: Design for someone
goals: Find out what a user needs
Write design criteria

units.title: Choosing materials
goals: Choose materials for strength, cost, looks and the planet

units.title: Inventors and engineers
goals: Describe famous inventions and the people who made them

subjects.title: Projects
subjects.framework: Finland's modules, Japan's integrated study, the IB and Cambridge Global Perspectives

units.title: A museum of the first civilisations
standards: IB PYP Where we are in place and time
goals: Build a museum room for each civilisation with an object and its label

units.title: A river town
goals: Plan and build a town by a river with bridges, fields and a mill
Work out areas

units.title: A light and sound show
goals: Wire lights and switches, then play a tune on the game's instruments
